newsitem.title: OMAN: Omani officials give up jobs as company directors.
newsitem.headline: Omani officials give up jobs as company directors.

text.p: Some 23 senior Omani government officials have had to resign as directors of private sector companies in line with the country's new constitution, the stock exchange president said in remarks published on Wednesday.

"Twenty-three ministers or officials of ministerial rank were informed that they had to resign as chairmen or members of the boards of directors of 41 publicly-held companies," Muscat Securities Market executive president Mahmoud al-Jarwani said, as quoted by the daily Oman.
The paper said the officials stepped down in accordance with Oman's "basic law", the Gulf oil state's first written constitution which was issued earlier this month.
The constitution prohibits ministers from serving as directors in publicly-held firms, saying the measure would help ensure they do "not exploit their positions for personal gain".
"Some of the companies have elected new chairmen while others are asking shareholders to elect new boards of directors," Jarwani said.
Some 94 companies are listed on the Muscat bourse, the most open of all Gulf exchanges.
